supporting_docs: 2.1 Lease - 1850 Oak Ridge Parkway Zionsville (Kowalczyk Family Realty).pdf
2.2 First Amendment to Lease - Zionsville (Market Rent at Closing).pdf
2.3 Northfield Commercial Advisors - Opinion of Market Rent - Zionsville.pdf
question_topics: Whether the closing-date rent in the amendment is binding (it is void if no closing by December 31, 2026)
Comparability of the broker's absolute-net market rent with the existing lease basis (tenant pays taxes, insurance and maintenance)
Post-close lease term and the 2.5% escalator from the first anniversary of closing in the buyer's run-rate
adjustments.rationale: Tied 6100 to 29 monthly Kowalczyk Family Realty bills of $32.0k for 1850 Oak Ridge Pkwy ($384.0k a year; Reference KFR-Z and the memo identify Zionsville, separate from the $6.0k Noblesville rent paid to the same landlord). The executed 2021 lease fixes rent at $32.0k a month, absolute net, no escalation. Northfield's opinion of market rent (no interest in the property, fee not contingent) concludes $19.60/RSF absolute net on 15,000 RSF, i.e. $294.0k a year ($24.5k a month), and the landlord has signed an amendment resetting rent to $24.5k at closing. Normalization = $384.0k - $294.0k = $90.0k in each period. The Company pays the building's real estate taxes directly (6800, May/Nov installments), consistent with the absolute-net lease and benchmark, so the rents compare like for like. Executed lease plus an independent benchmark: accept.
adjustments.reviewer_note: Normalization positive control (D1 made every normalization REQUEST_INFO). Must not fire: NORMALIZATION_BENCHMARK_MISSING, UNSIGNED_OR_DRAFT_SUPPORT, RECURRING_PATTERN (recurrence is the premise), OVERLAP_WITH_OTHER_ADJUSTMENT (the KFR-N Noblesville rows belong to A-2). Normalized to year-1 market cash rent per the Northfield opinion (standard QoE practice). The amendment extends the term 10 years from closing with 2.5% escalators; straight-line expense would be about $329.4k a year (normalization about $54.6k on that basis). That is a buyer GAAP run-rate consideration, not pre-registered. The benchmark is a seller-commissioned SIOR broker opinion (no interest in the property, fee not contingent), which the D1 case list accepts for this control.

question_topics: Confirmation that the $9,250 amended rent is the rent the buyer will bear from closing
Any other related-party arrangements on non-market terms (services, equipment, parking)

The executed 2019 lease fixes rent at $6.0k a month, absolute net, and says it was set to help open the clinic, not by survey. Brightwater's MAI appraisal (effective 2/1/26, no interest, fee not contingent) concludes $18.50/SF absolute net on 6,000 SF, i.e. $111.0k a year ($9.25k a month), and the signed amendment resets rent to $9.25k at closing. Normalization = $72.0k - $111.0k = -$39.0k in each period. The Company pays the building's real estate taxes directly (6800, May/Nov installments), consistent with the absolute-net lease and benchmark, so the rents compare like for like. Management's own EBITDA-reducing adjustment is supported by an appraisal and an executed amendment: accept the negative amount.
adjustments.reviewer_note: Must not fire: SIGN_ERROR (a negative normalization of expense rows is correct, not a sign conflict), NORMALIZATION_BENCHMARK_MISSING, RECURRING_PATTERN. REQUEST_INFO or dropping the item overstates every period by $39.0k.

3.2 Lease Termination Agreement - Brownsburg Clinic (Eagle Creek).pdf

5.7 Tate Whitcomb Invoice TW-26-0312 (Matters 4468 and 4471).pdf
question_topics: Payroll of the two clinicians transferred to Avon (Metro South & West clinical payroll up about $17k/month from March 2026) and Brownsburg patient visits and revenue retained at Avon since March 2026
Stranded costs left in EBITDA (regional director, EMR enterprise subscription, billing office) and whether any end after closing
Employer payroll taxes and benefits for Brownsburg staff, excluded from the claim (seller upside)
Post-closure Brownsburg receivable collections, the $9,400 security deposit refund and any remaining lease obligations
adjustments.rationale: Brownsburg (acquired 2022) posts revenue monthly from its legacy billing system (4000/4010) and has its own payroll journals (5000), Suite 110 rent (6100) and utility account (6120), so its results are identifiable in the GL. Net loss per the GL: FY24 $116.0k, FY25 $177.8k; TTM $160.8k operating loss (Jun-25 to the April 2026 final utility bill) plus $52.65k of closure costs (termination fee $38.25k under the executed 3/2/26 agreement, Tate Whitcomb Matter 4471 $4.35k on split invoice TW-26-0312, equipment move $3.2k, final pay and PTO $6.85k) = $213.5k. The closure has happened: last patient day 2/27/26, lease terminated 3/31/26, no Brownsburg-coded postings after the final bill. Shared costs that continue (regional director, EMR enterprise fee, billing office, central supplies, employer taxes and benefits) are correctly left in EBITDA. Management's amounts tie to the GL: accept. The termination fee is carried here, not in A-15.
adjustments.reviewer_note: Realized pro forma positive control. Must not fire: PRO_FORMA_NOT_REALIZED (Brownsburg activity stops), SIGN_ERROR (revenue credits inside a net-loss add-back), RECURRING_PATTERN, OVERLAP_WITH_OTHER_ADJUSTMENT on A-3 (A-3 keeps the termination fee: A-15's entire claim is inside A-3, so A-15 is the duplicate; the Matter 4471 row of TW-26-0312 is a different GL row from A-5's Matter 4468 row). Two of five Brownsburg clinicians moved to Avon on 3/2/26 with their patients (3.6). Metro South & West clinical payroll is about $17k/month higher from Mar-26 (trend-adjusted). The full-P&L removal assumes the revenue those clinicians and the other retained patients generate at Avon (R) covers their continuing cost (C): pro forma = reported + A-3 + R - C. At Brownsburg's revenue-to-clinical-payroll ratio (about 0.9), R - C for the two clinicians is about -$1.5k/month, and Brownsburg patients absorbed by Avon's existing therapists add revenue without cost. The sign is uncertain and the size small, so no alternative amount is registered. Joint alternative with A-15: see A-15. Unclaimed employer taxes and benefits on the three eliminated positions (about $25k a year; the two transferred clinicians' taxes continue) are seller upside.

adjustments.rationale: Hoosier Relocation invoice HRS-25-0814 posts as three GL lines. The move crews ($18.4k) and equipment disconnect and reinstall ($9.6k) are one-time relocation costs, as is the Monon cabling ($6.5k in the GL). The third line ($3.45k, 6100) is Aug-Oct 2025 storage at $1,150 a month; the invoice says storage continues month to month until items are released, and HRS has billed $1,150 every month since November 2025 (unclaimed). Storage is a continuing cost, not part of the move: removed. Separately, Monon's invoice totals $6,955.00 with $182 freight and $273 sales tax, but only $6,500.00 is in the GL: carry the GL amount and ask where the difference went. question_topics: Status and timing of the $31,850 insurance recovery on claim PSM-26-004417 (after the $10,000 deductible)
Treatment of the $31,850 insurance receivable (probable at May 31, 2026 but unrecorded) in closing working capital, and exclusion of the cash recovery from post-close EBITDA
Revenue lost while the Fishers clinic was closed (January 26 to February 6, 2026) and any business income claim
adjustments.rationale: Burst-pipe damage at Fishers on 1/24/26: Circle City Restoration $24.6k (Feb-26) and Hamilton County Flooring & Drywall $17.25k (Mar-26), both citing claim PSM-26-004417, tie to 6150. Casualty repair, non-recurring: add back $41.85k in TTM. Prairie State Mutual confirmed coverage on 4/8/26 and estimates a $31.85k payment after the $10k deductible; the sworn proof of loss was filed 5/12/26 and payment is expected in June. The recovery was probable at 5/31/26, so an accrual close could have recognized a $31.85k receivable in TTM, but nothing is recorded in the GL. Relative to the GL the full $41.85k is added back; accruing the recovery (+$31.85k) and adding back only the $10k net loss gives the same TTM EBITDA. The unrecorded receivable is a working-capital item. Accept unchanged.
adjustments.reviewer_note: Pending-recovery trap. Must not fire: OFFSETTING_RECOVERY (no recovery is in the GL), RECURRING_PATTERN. Cutting the add-back by the expected $31,850 would understate TTM EBITDA: the cost is in TTM and the recovery is not.

supporting_docs: 10.1 Notice of Proposed Assessment - Use Tax Audit 2024.pdf
question_topics: Use tax on 2025 and 2026 out-of-state purchases (is the Company now self-assessing?) and any further exposure
Payment or protest of the assessment and any tax indemnity in the purchase agreement
Whether penalty abatement was requested
Split of the $340,571.43 audited purchases between capitalized equipment and furniture and expensed supplies (use tax on capital items is capitalized)
adjustments.rationale: The notice of proposed assessment covers purchases from 1/1/24 to 12/31/24: tax $23,840, 10% negligence penalty $2,384 and interest $1,652, all booked 11/18/25. The tax is a 2024 cost booked in FY25: remove it from FY25 and TTM (+$23.84k) and record it in FY24 (-$23.84k). The penalty ($2.384k, 6800) is inside EBITDA and non-recurring: add back in FY25 and TTM. The interest ($1.652k) sits in 8100 Interest Expense, which reported EBITDA already excludes; adding it back double counts. Revised: FY24 -$23.84k, FY25 +$26.224k, TTM +$26.224k.
adjustments.reviewer_note: Two-sided out-of-period tax, an in-EBITDA penalty and already-excluded interest in one assessment. Must not fire: RECURRING_PATTERN. Only the tax row moves to FY2024: the penalty is a non-recurring charge of the November 2025 assessment and is added back where booked (FY2024 -26,224 is wrong). FY2024 -23,840 is an upper bound: use tax on capitalized equipment and furniture belongs in asset cost, not FY2024 opex. No use-tax self-assessment appears in 2025-26, so unassessed 2025-26 use tax (about $24k a year at the 2024 rate) is a debt-like, indemnity and run-rate item, not quantifiable from the package.

Contract therapy labour recurs (Summit Allied per diem continues, including Lafayette coverage of $20,980.18 in FY2025), but the claim is a cut-off correction, not a non-recurrence claim, so recurrence is no ground to reject (§5.4 exemption for OUT_OF_PERIOD items).

question_topics: Midstate revenue in TTM ($46,350, Jun-Aug 2025) that will not recur (lost customer)
Credit exposure and concentration in the other employer onsite contracts
Any distribution expected from the receivership
adjustments.rationale: Midstate Employer Health Network went into receivership on 9/22/25 and the receiver expects nothing for unsecured creditors. Kinetic Ridge's claim form lists the three unpaid Jun-Aug 2025 onsite invoices ($15,450 each, $46,350), which tie to the Nov-25 write-off in 6950. Routine patient write-offs run $1.9k-$3.7k a month (about $2.7k on average). A customer-specific loss of this size is non-recurring: accept in full.
adjustments.reviewer_note: False-reject trap: one large write-off among small routine entries in the same account. Must not fire: RECURRING_PATTERN. The >=50% other-fiscal-period leg must be judged on theme, not account: FY2024 6950 is $32,503 (70% of the claim) but is entirely patient balances sent to collections, a different theme from an employer customer's receivership. The >=3-month leg fails the 25% floor. Pre-registered alternative: REVISE -19,240.17 / +26,101.83 / +27,521.83 (6950 at its 29-month average, $51,743.17 a year). Buyer view, not registered: the Jun-Aug 2025 Midstate revenue ($46,350, rows 921/927/933) never converted to cash and the customer ceased operations on 9/19/25, so accepting the add-back leaves $46,350 of uncollected revenue from a defunct customer in TTM.
